description: Example Charts renders a chart from inline data and returns it as static SVG, or a complete HTML document, inside a JSON object. POST /v1/chart with data (csv, tsv, json, or values) plus either a full Vega-Lite v6 spec or the shorthand form (type, x, y, color, size, shape, theta, ranges, colors, theme). Every data mark carries a native <title> tooltip, so no script is returned or required. Remote data URLs are refused; all inputs live in the request body. Output is deterministic for identical input on the same version. Limits (1 MiB body, 50k rows, 10k marks by default) are reported by GET /v1/capabilities.

rpc_types.notes: POST /v1/chart, GET /v1/version, GET /healthz, GET /v1/capabilities, and GET /v1/openapi.json are expected. Every response is a JSON object; the SVG or HTML rides in the 'html' string field, always last.

specs.notes: The same document is served by the backend at GET /v1/openapi.json. Add sha256 once the URL is frozen.

serving.backend: The example-charts container (Node 22, Vega 6, Vega-Lite 6; built from services/example-charts/backend) behind the HA RelayMiner with the rest backend pointed at it. No auth toward the backend; callers cannot send headers. CPU-bound; about 150 MB RAM per render worker (PC_WORKERS, default 2). Caps are PC_* environment variables.

healthcheck.notes: Identity probe: pins the backend to this service so a wrong backend cannot be staked under this id.
Readiness probe: 200 only once a render worker is up.
Functional probe: renders one bar and reports one data mark. Cheap and deterministic.

serving.notes: Every request is a POST JSON body to /v1/chart; typical renders finish in well under a second. No rate limits to disable. Gateway operators: configure as type passthrough with rpc_types ["rest"] and a relay_timeout of at least 15s; see sage-service.yaml in the service repository.
